mainTopic: False oaths of a שוכר and a שואל, and whether a שומר who hands the item to another שומר is liable.
overview: This amud finishes רבי ירמיה's list of the קרבנות a שוכר and a שואל bring when they swear falsely about a cow. The גמרא gives the rule behind the list: a lie that denies money owed brings an אשם, and a lie that changes nothing about payment brings a חטאת. It then works through all four combinations. It explains that the list teaches that the הלכה is not like רבי אמי: an oath imposed by judges still counts as a שבועת ביטוי. Next comes a new dispute about a שומר who hands the item to another שומר. רב says he is exempt, and רבי יוחנן says he is liable, because the owner can say 'I don't want my deposit in someone else's hand.' רב חסדא shows that רב's view was only inferred from a story about gardeners' spades, and that the story had a special detail. Finally, רבי יוחנן's view is challenged from two משניות. The first challenge is answered, and רבא begins answering the second, with his answer continuing on the next amud.

steps.title: רבי ירמיה finishes his list of possible outcomes
steps.stepSummary: רבי ירמיה lists the remaining combinations. Sometimes both bring an אשם. Sometimes the שוכר brings a חטאת and the שואל an אשם. Sometimes it is the other way around.
steps.simpleTranslation: Sometimes both bring a guilt-offering. Sometimes the renter brings a sin-offering and the borrower a guilt-offering. Sometimes the renter brings a guilt-offering and the borrower a sin-offering.
steps.whatsHappening: רבי ירמיה is finishing a list of every possible outcome when a שוכר and a שואל both swear falsely about the same cow. This sets up the explanations that come next.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבי ירמיה is telling us that the same lie can bring different קרבנות for a שוכר and a שואל. The reason is that each type of guardian pays in different situations. So whether a lie actually 'cost' the owner money depends on who told it.

keyTerms.meaning: Guilt-offering, brought for a false oath that denied money
Sin-offering, brought here for a false oath that did not affect money
Renter, a paid guardian. He pays for theft or loss, but not for accidents beyond his control
Borrower. He pays for almost everything, even accidents beyond his control

phrases.english: Sometimes both bring a guilt-offering.
Sometimes the renter brings a sin-offering
and the borrower a guilt-offering,
sometimes the renter brings a guilt-offering
and the borrower a sin-offering.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Continues רבי ירמיה's list from the previous amud, which began with 'both bring a חטאת.'
steps.mimraCoreRuling: A false oath by a שוכר and a שואל can lead to any combination of אשם and חטאת.

steps.title: The key rule: money denied means אשם, empty words mean חטאת
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא gives the rule behind all of רבי ירמיה's cases. A false oath that denies money brings an אשם. A false oath that is only empty words, with no money at stake, brings a חטאת.
steps.simpleTranslation: How is this? Denying money brings a guilt-offering. An empty statement of the lips brings a sin-offering.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא asks how רבי ירמיה's different outcomes come about. It answers with one simple rule that explains every case.
steps.deeperAnalysis: There are two kinds of false oath here. If the lie gets you out of paying money you really owe, it is כפירת ממון, and you bring an אשם. If the lie changes nothing about what you pay, it is just ביטוי שפתיים, and you bring a חטאת.

keyTerms.meaning: How so? A request to explain
Denying money that you really owe
An oath that is only words, with no money at stake

steps.whatToRemember: The test for every case is simple. Did the lie save the guardian money he really owed? If yes, he brings an אשם. If no, he brings a חטאת.

phrases.english: How is this?
Denial of money: a guilt-offering.
An utterance of the lips: a sin-offering.
phrases.notes: A false oath that did not take any money from anyone.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Gives the rule that explains the list in step 1.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: A false oath that denies money brings an אשם. A false oath of empty words brings a חטאת.

steps.title: Case where both bring a חטאת: the cow died naturally, but they claimed an accident
steps.stepSummary: The cow died a natural death, but both guardians swore it died through an accident beyond their control. The lie did not change what either one pays, so both bring a חטאת.
steps.simpleTranslation: Sometimes both bring a sin-offering. This is when the cow died naturally, and they said it died through an accident beyond their control. The renter is exempt either way, so he brings a sin-offering. The borrower must pay either way, so he brings a sin-offering.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא explains the case where both bring a חטאת. Each lie made no difference to what the guardian owes.
steps.deeperAnalysis: For a שוכר, both a natural death and an accident are beyond his control, so he pays nothing either way. For a שואל, he pays for both, so he owes the same either way. Since neither lie saved any money, each oath is just ביטוי שפתיים, and each brings a חטאת.

keyTerms.meaning: It was lost through an accident beyond his control
Exempt, does not have to pay

steps.confusionAlert: Do not think that a lie is less serious just because it is a חטאת. The oath here was still false. It just did not take money from the owner, so it is a different kind of sin.

phrases.english: Sometimes both bring a sin-offering:
for example, where it died naturally,
and they said it died through an accident beyond their control.
The renter, who either way
is exempt, brings a sin-offering,
the borrower, who either way
is liable to pay, brings a sin-offering.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Applies the rule from step 2 to the case where both bring a חטאת.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: A natural death that they claimed was an accident. Neither guardian's payment changes, so both bring a חטאת.

steps.title: Case where both bring an אשם: the cow was stolen, but they claimed it died from work
steps.stepSummary: The cow was stolen, which both guardians must pay for. But both swore it died from normal work, which would free them from paying. Each one denied money he really owed, so both bring an אשם.
steps.simpleTranslation: Sometimes both bring a guilt-offering. This is when the cow was stolen, and they said it died from work. Both are denying money, because they really owe it, and they are trying to free themselves.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא explains the case where both bring an אשם. Each lie got the guardian out of a payment he truly owed.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Both the שוכר and the שואל must pay when the cow is stolen. Both are exempt if it died from normal work. By lying, each one moved himself from 'owes money' to 'owes nothing.' That is כפירת ממון, so each brings an אשם.

keyTerms.meaning: It died because of the normal work it was used for

steps.whatToRemember: Compare this with step 3. In step 3, the lie did not change the payment, so both brought a חטאת. Here, the lie wiped out a real debt, so both bring an אשם.

phrases.english: Sometimes both bring a guilt-offering:
for example, where it was stolen,
and they said it died because of the work,
since both of them are denying money,
for they really are liable,
and they are freeing themselves.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Repeats the 'both bring an אשם' line from step 1 so it can explain it. It applies the rule from step 2.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: The cow was stolen, but they claimed it died from work. Both deny a real debt, so both bring an אשם.

steps.title: Renter brings a sin-offering, borrower brings a guilt-offering
steps.stepSummary: The cow died naturally, but both guardians swore it died from normal work. The שוכר brings a חטאת, and the שואל brings an אשם.
steps.simpleTranslation: Sometimes the renter brings a sin-offering and the borrower brings a guilt-offering. This happens when the cow died naturally, but they both said it died from work. The renter is free from paying either way, so he brings a sin-offering. The borrower has to pay when it dies naturally, but he tried to free himself by saying it died from work. So he brings a guilt-offering.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא explains the case where the same lie gives the שוכר a חטאת but the שואל an אשם.
steps.deeperAnalysis: A שוכר does not pay when an animal dies naturally, and he does not pay when it dies from work either. His lie changed nothing about money, so it is a שבועת ביטוי and he brings a חטאת. A שואל does pay for a natural death but not for death from work, so his lie denied money he owed, and he brings an אשם.

phrases.english: The renter brings a sin-offering and the borrower a guilt-offering –
such as where it died a natural death,
and they said it died because of work.

phrases.aramaic: שׂוֹכֵר דְּבֵין כָּךְ וּבֵין כָּךְ מִיפְּטַר פָּטוּר –
phrases.english: The renter, who is exempt either way –
phrases.notes: A renter does not pay for a natural death, and no guardian pays for death from work, so the lie changed nothing for him.

phrases.english: is liable to bring a sin-offering.
The borrower, who must pay when it dies naturally,

phrases.aramaic: וְקָא פָטַר נַפְשֵׁיהּ בְּמֵתָה מֵחֲמַת מְלָאכָה – בְּאָשָׁם.
phrases.english: and he freed himself by saying it died from work – brings a guilt-offering.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Third case on רבי ירמיה's list, after the two cases where both guardians bring the same offering.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: In what case does the שוכר bring a חטאת while the שואל brings an אשם?
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: When the cow died naturally and both swore it died from work.

steps.title: Renter brings a guilt-offering, borrower brings a sin-offering
steps.stepSummary: The cow was stolen, but both guardians swore it died naturally. The שוכר brings an אשם, and the שואל brings a חטאת.
steps.simpleTranslation: Sometimes the renter brings a guilt-offering and the borrower a sin-offering. This happens when the cow was stolen, but they both said it died naturally. The renter has to pay for theft and loss, but he tried to free himself by claiming a natural death, so he brings a guilt-offering. The borrower has to pay either way, so he brings a sin-offering.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא explains the reverse case, where the שוכר brings an אשם and the שואל brings a חטאת.
steps.deeperAnalysis: A שוכר pays for theft but not for a natural death, so his lie tried to cancel a real debt, and he brings an אשם. A שואל pays for theft and for a natural death alike. His lie saved him nothing, so it counts only as empty words, and he brings a חטאת.
steps.whatToRemember: The same lie can give one guardian a חטאת and another an אשם. It all depends on whether that guardian's lie got him out of paying.

phrases.english: The renter brings a guilt-offering and the borrower a sin-offering –
such as where it was stolen, and they said it died naturally.
The renter is the one who must pay for theft and loss,

phrases.aramaic: וְקָא פָטַר נַפְשֵׁיהּ בְּמֵתָה כְּדַרְכָּהּ – בְּאָשָׁם.
phrases.english: and he freed himself by saying it died naturally – brings a guilt-offering.

phrases.aramaic: שׁוֹאֵל דְּבֵין כָּךְ וּבֵין כָּךְ חַיּוֹבֵי מִיחַיַּיב – בְּחַטָּאת.
phrases.english: The borrower, who must pay either way – brings a sin-offering.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: The mirror image of step 5. It completes the list of all four combinations.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: In what case does the שוכר bring an אשם while the שואל brings a חטאת?
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: When the cow was stolen and both swore it died naturally.

steps.title: What does this list teach us?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks what new idea this list of cases is teaching, since every case simply follows the known rules.
steps.simpleTranslation: What is it teaching us?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא asks why this list was needed at all. This sets up the answer in the next step.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Each case just applies the basic rules of guardians and oaths. So the גמרא wants to know what new point is hidden inside the list.

phrases.english: What is it teaching us?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Looks back at the whole list in steps 1 to 6 and asks what it adds.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: What new teaching does the detailed list contain?

steps.title: The list rejects the view of רבי אמי
steps.stepSummary: רבי אמי held that an oath imposed by judges cannot make someone liable for a שבועת ביטוי, because the פסוק speaks of someone who swears on his own. The list shows that this is not the הלכה, because here a guardian who swore in court does bring a חטאת.
steps.simpleTranslation: It comes to exclude the view of רבי אמי, who said: any oath that the judges make a person swear does not make him liable for a שבועת ביטוי. The פסוק says, 'Or if a person swears, saying with his lips,' and 'if he swears' means on his own. The list teaches us that the הלכה is not like רבי אמי.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers that the list was taught to reject רבי אמי's opinion.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The guardians' oaths here were imposed by the judges. רבי אמי would say that a lie with no money at stake in such an oath carries no קרבן at all. The list rules that it does bring a חטאת as a שבועת ביטוי, so it disagrees with רבי אמי.

keyTerms.meaning: an oath of speech, which brings a חטאת if false

steps.whatToRemember: The הלכה is not like רבי אמי. A person who swears falsely in court, even with no money at stake, still brings a חטאת for a שבועת ביטוי.
steps.confusionAlert: Don't think the list was only practice in the rules of guardians. Its real point is that a court-imposed oath still counts as a שבועת ביטוי.

phrases.english: It comes to exclude the view of רבי אמי, who said:
Any oath that the judges make a person swear –

phrases.aramaic: אֵין חַיָּיבִין עָלֶיהָ מִשּׁוּם שְׁבוּעַת בִּיטּוּי,
phrases.english: one is not liable for it as an oath of speech,
as it says: 'Or if a person swears'
'saying with his lips'
'If he swears' means on his own.

phrases.aramaic: קָא מַשְׁמַע לַן דְּלָא כְּרַבִּי אַמֵּי.
phrases.english: It teaches us that the halacha is not like רבי אמי.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the question in step 7.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: What new teaching does the list contain?
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: That a court-imposed oath can still bring a חטאת as a שבועת ביטוי, against רבי אמי.
steps.maskanaFinalTakeaway: The הלכה is not like רבי אמי.

steps.title: A guardian who handed the item to another guardian
steps.stepSummary: A new topic opens. A שומר handed the item he was guarding to another שומר. רב says he is exempt, and רבי יוחנן says he is liable.
steps.simpleTranslation: It was said: a guardian who handed the item over to another guardian. רב said he is exempt, and רבי יוחנן said he is liable.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא starts a new discussion and quotes a dispute between רב and רבי יוחנן. This sets up the back-and-forth that follows.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The question is whether passing the item to a second guardian changes the first guardian's responsibility. רב holds that he stays exempt. רבי יוחנן holds that he is liable. The reasons for each view will come in the next steps.

keyTerms.meaning: it was said (introduces a dispute between אמוראים)
a guardian who handed the item to another guardian

phrases.english: It was said: a guardian who handed the item to another guardian,
רב said: he is exempt,
and רבי יוחנן said: he is liable.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Starts a new topic about guardians, separate from the discussion of oaths.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Dispute: רב says a guardian who handed the item to another guardian is exempt; רבי יוחנן says he is liable.

steps.title: אביי: How far רב's exemption goes
steps.stepSummary: אביי explains that according to רב, the first שומר is exempt even when he hands the item to a lower-level guardian, because he gave it to a responsible person.
steps.simpleTranslation: אביי said: According to רב, you don't even need to say that a שומר חנם who hands the item to a שומר שכר is exempt, since he upgraded its protection. Even a שומר שכר who hands it to a שומר חנם, and so lowered its protection, is exempt. Why? Because he gave it to a responsible, sensible person.
steps.whatsHappening: אביי is measuring how far רב's ruling from Step 9 reaches. He says רב exempts the first guardian even in the weaker case, where the item ends up with a lower-level guardian.
steps.deeperAnalysis: A שומר שכר owes more than a שומר חנם, so handing the item from a שומר חנם to a שומר שכר upgrades its protection, and handing it the other way downgrades it. רב exempts in both directions. For רב, what matters is only that the item went to a responsible person (בן דעת), not what level of guardian that person is.

keyTerms.meaning: According to his line of reasoning
Not only... but even (from the easier case to the bigger case)

steps.confusionAlert: Watch the word order: שומר חנם to שומר שכר is the UPGRADE (the easy case for רב), and שומר שכר to שומר חנם is the DOWNGRADE (the big חידוש for רב).

phrases.english: Abaye said: according to Rav's reasoning,
it does not need to be said that an unpaid guardian
who handed it over to a paid guardian
since he upgraded its protection,
phrases.notes: A paid guardian must pay in more situations, so the item is now better protected.

phrases.english: but even a paid guardian
who handed it over to an unpaid guardian,
where he downgraded its protection, is exempt.
What is the reason?
Because he handed it over to a responsible person.

steps.triggerLanguage: אמר אביי לטעמיה דרב לא מבעיא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Explains the full reach of רב's side of the dispute in Step 9.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: According to רב, a שומר who hands the item to another שומר is exempt even if the second one is a lower-level guardian, because he gave it to a בן דעת.

steps.title: אביי: How far רבי יוחנן's liability goes
steps.stepSummary: According to רבי יוחנן, the first שומר is liable even when he hands the item to a higher-level guardian, because the owner can say he did not want his item with someone else.
steps.simpleTranslation: And according to רבי יוחנן, you don't even need to say that a שומר שכר who hands the item to a שומר חנם is liable, since he lowered its protection. Even a שומר חנם who hands it to a שומר שכר, and so upgraded its protection, is liable. Because the owner can say to him: I do not want my deposit to be in someone else's hands.
steps.whatsHappening: אביי now does the same for רבי יוחנן. He shows that רבי יוחנן holds the first guardian liable even in the upgrade case.
steps.deeperAnalysis: For רבי יוחנן, the level of protection does not matter at all. The owner trusted this specific person, and he has the right to say he does not want anyone else holding his item. So passing it on, even to a better guardian, is already a breach.

keyTerms.meaning: An item left with someone for safekeeping

steps.whatToRemember: רב looks at whether the item went to a responsible person (בן דעת), so he exempts in both directions. רבי יוחנן looks at the owner's wishes ("אין רצוני שיהא פקדוני ביד אחר"), so he holds the guardian liable in both directions.

phrases.english: And according to Rabbi Yochanan's reasoning,
it does not need to be said that a paid guardian
who handed it over to an unpaid guardian
since he downgraded its protection,
but even an unpaid guardian
who handed it over to a paid guardian,
where he upgraded its protection, is liable.
Because the owner can say to him:
"I do not want my deposit to be in someone else's hand."

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Parallel to Step 10, now for רבי יוחנן's side.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: According to רבי יוחנן, a שומר who hands the item to another שומר is liable even if the second one is a higher-level guardian, because the owner did not agree to anyone else holding it.

steps.title: רב חסדא: רב's ruling was only inferred
steps.stepSummary: רב חסדא says that רב never actually said this rule outright. People figured it out from another ruling of his.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב חסדא said: This ruling of רב was not said directly. It was inferred from something else.
steps.whatsHappening: רב חסדא questions where רב's opinion comes from. He is setting up a story that shows how people came to think רב holds this.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Until now we took for granted that רב clearly ruled that a שומר who passes the item on is exempt. רב חסדא says this was only a conclusion people drew from a case. That opens the door to asking whether the conclusion was correct.

keyTerms.meaning: By inference, worked out from something else

phrases.english: Rav Chisda said:
This ruling of Rav was not stated explicitly,
but was inferred.

steps.triggerLanguage: אמר רב חסדא הא דרב לאו בפירוש אתמר אלא מכללא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Moves from explaining רב's view to asking where that view actually comes from.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: רב's ruling that a שומר who passes the item to another שומר is exempt was not said outright. It was inferred.

steps.title: The story of the gardeners' spades
steps.stepSummary: Gardeners usually left their spades with an old woman. One day they left them with one gardener, who went off to a wedding and left them with the old woman. The spades were stolen.
steps.simpleTranslation: There were some gardeners who left their spades every day with a certain old woman. One day they left them with one of the gardeners. He heard the sound of a wedding, went out and left. He left the spades with that old woman. While he was away and coming back, the spades were stolen.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא tells the story that רב's ruling came from. This sets up the case that רב will rule on in the next step.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Here the gardener is the שומר, and he passed the spades on to a second guardian, the old woman. That makes it look like a classic case of שומר שמסר לשומר. Remember one key detail: the owners themselves left their spades with this same old woman every day.

phrases.english: For there were these gardeners,
who every day would leave their spades
with a certain old woman.

phrases.aramaic: יוֹמָא חַד אַפְקְדֻינְהוּ לְגַבֵּי חַד מִינַּיְיהוּ,
phrases.english: One day they left them with one of them,
phrases.notes: "One of them" means one of the gardeners, not the old woman.

phrases.english: he heard the sound of a wedding
and went out and left.
He left them with that old woman,
and while he went and came back
their spades were stolen.

steps.triggerLanguage: דהנהו גינאי דכל יומא הוו מפקדי מרייהו
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Supplies the case that רב חסדא says רב's view was inferred from.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Sets out the facts: a gardener who was guarding spades left them with the old woman the owners usually used, and they were stolen.

steps.title: רב exempts the gardener and people draw a conclusion
steps.stepSummary: רב exempted the gardener. Whoever saw the ruling thought the reason was that a שומר who passes the item to another שומר is exempt.
steps.simpleTranslation: The case came before רב, and he exempted the gardener. Someone who saw this thought it was because a שומר who hands the item to another שומר is exempt.
steps.whatsHappening: רב rules that the gardener does not pay, and observers turn this into a general rule. This is the "inference" רב חסדא mentioned in Step 12.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רב's actual words were only "exempt" for this specific case. The general rule "שומר שמסר לשומר פטור" is the observers' explanation of why. The next step will question that explanation.

phrases.english: He came before Rav, and Rav exempted him.
Whoever saw this thought
it was because a guardian who handed over to another guardian is exempt.

steps.triggerLanguage: אתא לקמיה דרב ופטריה מאן דחזא סבר
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Gives רב's ruling on the story and the general rule people drew from it.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: רב exempted the gardener, and observers took this to mean that a שומר who passes the item to another שומר is exempt.

steps.title: Not so: the owners themselves used that old woman
steps.stepSummary: רב חסדא rejects the inference. The spades case was special, because the owners themselves left their spades with that old woman every day.
steps.simpleTranslation: But that is not so. There it is different, because every day the owners themselves would leave their spades with that old woman.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא pushes back on the conclusion people drew from רב's ruling. It explains that רב exempted the gardener for a different reason.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבי יוחנן's reason for liability is that the owner can say "I do not want my item with someone else." Here the owners cannot say that, since they trusted this exact old woman every day. So רב's ruling fits even the view that a שומר who passes the item on is normally liable, and it gives no proof for a general exemption.
steps.whatToRemember: רב's ruling about the spades does not prove that a שומר may pass the item to another שומר. The gardener was exempt only because the owners themselves always trusted that same old woman.
steps.whyThisMatters: This takes away the only source for רב's supposed view. It shows that a ruling on a specific story can't be stretched into a general rule if the story has a special detail.

phrases.english: But that is not so.
There it is different,
because every day they themselves

phrases.aramaic: גַּבַּהּ דְּהַהִיא סָבְתָּא הֲווֹ מַפְקְדִי לְהוּ.
phrases.english: would leave them with that old woman.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Rejects the general rule that observers drew in Step 14.
steps.dechiyaRejectionScope: Rejects the inference that רב holds a שומר who passes the item to another שומר is always exempt.
steps.dechiyaFlawIdentified: The spades case had a special detail: the owners themselves trusted that old woman, so they could not object to the spades being with her.

steps.title: Challenge from the renter who lent out the cow
steps.stepSummary: רבי אמי teaches רבי יוחנן's rule, and רבי אבא בר ממל challenges it from a משנה. In that משנה a renter lends the cow to a borrower, and the renter is not held liable for passing it on.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי אמי sat and taught this rule. רבי אבא בר ממל challenged him from a משנה: Someone rents a cow and lends it to another person, and the cow dies naturally. The renter swears it died naturally, and the borrower pays the renter. But if רבי יוחנן is right, the owner should be able to say: 'I didn't want my deposit in someone else's hand!'
steps.whatsHappening: רבי אמי repeats רבי יוחנן's rule, and רבי אבא בר ממל attacks it using a משנה about a rented cow that was lent to someone else.
steps.deeperAnalysis: In the משנה, the renter gave the cow to a borrower, and the renter just swears and goes free. If רבי יוחנן were right, the owner could say he never agreed to let anyone else hold his cow, so the renter should have to pay. The משנה does not say this, so it seems to go against רבי יוחנן.

keyTerms.meaning: A teaching or rule (here, רבי יוחנן's rule)
He challenged him from a source
A renter, someone who pays to use an item
A borrower, someone who uses an item for free
Died naturally, in the normal way

keyTerms.term: אֵין רְצוֹנִי שֶׁיְּהֵא פִּקְדוֹנִי בְּיַד אַחֵר
keyTerms.meaning: 'I don't want my deposit in someone else's hand'

steps.confusionAlert: A renter does not pay when an animal dies naturally, but a borrower does. That is why the borrower pays the renter here while the renter only swears to the owner.

phrases.english: Rabbi Ami was sitting
and saying this teaching.
phrases.notes: This is רבי יוחנן's rule from before: the first שומר is liable even when he gives it to a better guardian.

phrases.aramaic: אֵיתִיבֵיהּ רַבִּי אַבָּא בַּר מֶמֶל לְרַבִּי אַמֵּי:
phrases.english: Rabbi Abba bar Memel challenged Rabbi Ami:
One who rents a cow from his friend
and lent it to another person
and it died in its normal way,
the renter swears that it died in its normal way
and the borrower pays the renter.
But if it is so (as רבי יוחנן said),
let the owner say to him:

phrases.aramaic: אֵין רְצוֹנִי שֶׁיְּהֵא פִּקְדוֹנִי בְּיַד אַחֵר!
phrases.english: I don't want my deposit to be in someone else's hand!

steps.triggerLanguage: אֵיתִיבֵיהּ רַבִּי אַבָּא בַּר מֶמֶל לְרַבִּי אַמֵּי
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Returns to רבי יוחנן's rule (step 11) and challenges it.
steps.kashyaTarget: רבי יוחנן's rule that a שומר who passes the item to another is liable because the owner can object.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: The משנה lets the renter go free after he lent the cow to someone else. If the owner could always object, the renter should be liable.

steps.title: The owner gave permission to lend
steps.stepSummary: רבי אמי answers that the משנה is talking about a case where the owner allowed the renter to lend the cow.
steps.simpleTranslation: He answered: What case are we dealing with here? A case where the owner gave the renter permission to lend it.
steps.whatsHappening: רבי אמי defends רבי יוחנן by limiting the משנה to a case where the owner said it was okay to lend.
steps.deeperAnalysis: If the owner gave permission, he cannot complain that his cow ended up with someone else. So the משנה does not go against רבי יוחנן. His rule still applies when there was no permission.

keyTerms.meaning: 'What case are we dealing with here?', which limits a source to a specific case

phrases.english: He said to him:
Here, what case are we dealing with?
Where the owner gave him permission to lend.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the challenge of step 16.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The משנה seemed to be talking about any renter who lent the cow.
steps.terutzMaskana: The משנה is only talking about a renter who had the owner's permission to lend.

steps.title: Then the borrower should pay the owner
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks: if the owner allowed the lending, the borrower should pay the owner directly, not the renter.
steps.simpleTranslation: If so, the borrower should have to pay the owner!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא pushes back on the answer. If the owner agreed to the lending, it looks as if the owner himself lent the cow, so the borrower should owe the owner.
steps.deeperAnalysis: With the owner's permission, the borrower would seem to be borrowing straight from the owner. But the משנה says the borrower pays the renter. That does not fit the answer of step 17.

phrases.english: If so,
he should have to pay the owner!
phrases.notes: The 'he' here is the borrower, who in the משנה pays the renter.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges the answer given in step 17.
steps.kashyaTarget: The explanation that the owner gave permission to lend.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: Permission from the owner would make the borrower owe the owner, but the משנה has him pay the renter.

steps.title: The owner said 'as you see fit'
steps.stepSummary: The answer is that the owner only told the renter to lend it if he saw fit, so the lending is still the renter's own decision.
steps.simpleTranslation: The owner told him: 'Lend it at your own discretion.'
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא sharpens the case. The owner allowed lending but left the choice to the renter.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Because the renter decided whether and to whom to lend, the borrower is dealing with the renter and pays him. The owner still cannot complain, because he did allow lending. So רבי יוחנן's rule stands.

keyTerms.meaning: At your discretion, as you decide

steps.whatToRemember: The first challenge is answered. The משנה is a case where the owner allowed lending 'at your discretion', so the owner cannot object, and the borrower pays the renter.

phrases.english: Where the owner said to him: 'At your discretion.'

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the challenge of step 18.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: Permission to lend means the owner himself is the lender.
steps.terutzMaskana: The permission was 'at your discretion', so the renter is the lender and the borrower pays him.

steps.title: Second challenge: coins given to small children
steps.stepSummary: רמי בר חמא brings a משנה that says a שומר is liable if he handed deposited coins to his small son or daughter, or guarded them in other careless ways.
steps.simpleTranslation: רמי בר חמא challenged: Someone deposited coins with a friend. If the friend tied them up and hung them behind his back, or handed them to his small son or daughter, or locked them up improperly, he is liable, because he did not guard the way guardians normally do.
steps.whatsHappening: This step sets up a new challenge. רמי בר חמא quotes a משנה, and the next step will draw the inference that attacks רבי יוחנן.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The משנה lists ways of guarding that are not good enough, including giving the coins to small children. The key detail is the word 'small' (קטנים). The גמרא will build its attack on that detail.

keyTerms.meaning: The normal way guardians watch things

phrases.english: Rami bar Chama challenged:
One who deposits coins with his friend,
and the friend tied them up and slung them behind his back,
or handed them to his young son or daughter,
or locked them up improperly,
he is liable, because he did not guard the way guardians do.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Opens a second challenge to רבי יוחנן's rule.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: The משנה only makes the guardian liable for giving the coins to small children. The inference from that comes in the next step.

steps.title: Grown children would be fine, so why can't the owner object?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא infers from the משנה that giving the coins to grown children would leave the guardian exempt. That goes against רבי יוחנן, who says the owner can object to anyone else holding his item.
steps.simpleTranslation: The reason he is liable is that they were small children. So if they were grown up, he would be exempt. But why? Let the owner say: 'I don't want my deposit in someone else's hand!'
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא finishes רמי בר חמא's challenge. It infers from the word 'small' that grown children would be okay, and that clashes with רבי יוחנן.
steps.deeperAnalysis: If handing the coins to anyone else were a problem, as רבי יוחנן says, the משנה would not need to mention small children at all. Grown children would also be 'someone else'. The משנה seems to allow passing the coins to responsible grown children, which goes against רבי יוחנן.

keyTerms.meaning: 'The reason is because', which sets up an inference from a detail
Exempt, does not have to pay

steps.confusionAlert: The משנה never says 'grown children are fine' in so many words. The גמרא is inferring it from the fact that the משנה specifically said 'small'.

phrases.english: The reason is that they were small children,
but with grown children, he would be exempt.
Why?
Let the owner say to him:

phrases.aramaic: אֵין רְצוֹנִי שֶׁיְּהֵא פִּקְדוֹנִי בְּיַד אַחֵר!
phrases.english: I don't want my deposit to be in someone else's hand!

steps.triggerLanguage: טַעְמָא דִּקְטַנִּים הָא גְּדוֹלִים פָּטוּר אַמַּאי
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Draws the inference from the משנה quoted in step 20 and completes the challenge.
steps.kashyaTarget: רבי יוחנן's rule that the owner can object to his item being with anyone else.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: The משנה implies that grown children may hold the coins, so passing the deposit to another person is not always a problem.

steps.title: רבא begins his answer about every depositor
steps.stepSummary: רבא starts to answer the challenge against רבי יוחנן with a general statement about anyone who deposits an item.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבא said: anyone who deposits an item…
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא is setting up the next move. רבא begins his answer to the challenge from the משנה by opening a general rule about any person who deposits an item with someone else.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The challenge was that the משנה lets a שומר hand the coins to grown children without being liable, which seems to clash with רבי יוחנן. רבא will not argue with the inference. Instead, he will explain what every depositor has in mind when he hands over his item. Only the opening words of that rule appear here; the actual content comes in the next lines.

keyTerms.meaning: An אמורא who gives the answer here
Anyone who deposits an item with someone else
The owner who leaves his item with a guardian

steps.confusionAlert: This is only the start of רבא's sentence. Don't treat it as his full answer yet. The rule he is building finishes in the next lines.

phrases.english: Rava said:
anyone who deposits an item,

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Opens the answer to the קשיא in step 21, which used the משנה to challenge רבי יוחנן.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Begins a general rule about what a depositor has in mind, which will explain the משנה's case without contradicting רבי יוחנן.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The משנה's exemption for giving the coins to grown children seems to show that a שומר may hand a deposit to others, against רבי יוחנן.
steps.terutzMaskana: Still in progress. רבא is setting up a rule about every depositor's assumptions, to be finished in the next lines.
